'''Franz Maximilian Matschinsky''' (July 17, 1931 – March 31, 2022) was a German-American medical doctor, [[pharmacologist]], and [[biochemist]]. He conducted research in the field of [[insulin]] secretion and [[diabetes]] therapy.<ref>{{cite web |title=In Memoriam of Dr. Franz Matschinsky |work=Perelman School of Medicine |url=https://www.med.upenn.edu/idom/memorial.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220429115411/https://www.med.upenn.edu/idom/memorial.html |archive-date=April 29, 2022 }}</ref>

==Life==
Franz M. Matschinsky was born on July 17, 1931, in [[Wrocław|Breslau]], then [[Former eastern territories of Germany|Germany]]. He initially grew up in the village of Rothbrünnig Kreis Goldberg (today [[Brennik, Złotoryja County]]) in [[Silesia]], where his parents managed a farm. He attended the municipal high school Herzog-Heinrich-Schule in [[Liegnitz]] until 1945. In 1946, as a result of the [[Flight and expulsion of Germans from Poland during and after World War II|expulsion]] after the [[Second World War]], the family ended up in the village of Westönnen near [[Werl]] ([[Soest, Germany|Soest]] district) in the [[Allied-occupied Germany#British Zone|British Zone]] of what was later [[West-Germany]]. Matschinsky continued his schooling at the Marien-Gymnasium Werl, where he graduated in 1953.

Matschinsky received a BS in Basic Medical Science from the [[University of Freiburg|Albert Ludwig University]]  (1953-1955) and then moved to [[LMU Munich]] (1955-1959). He received his M.D. in 1959 under [[Heinrich Otto Wieland]] on the topic of "On the mechanism of the [[Amanita phalloides]] toxin [[phalloidin]]". During his studies, he spent about one year under [[Feodor Lynen]]'s personal supervision at the [[Max Planck Institute]] of Cell Chemistry in Munich (1955/1956) as a scholarship holder of the German [[Studienstiftung]].

Two years as a [[postdoctoral fellow]] in Wieland's laboratory were followed by a period as a [[Internship (medicine)#Germany|medical intern]] at the Marienhospital in [[Hagen]] (1961-1963). During this time he married Elke Fritz<ref>https://www.lyonsfs.com/memorials/elke-matschinsky/4005714/index.php Obituary Elke Matschinsky</ref> to whom he was married until her death in 2019. The couple had a daughter and two sons. Shortly after the birth of their first child, he continued his scientific training with [[Oliver H. Lowry]] in the department of pharmacology at [[Washington University School of Medicine]] in [[St. Louis]], [[Missouri]], United States (1963-1965). At this university, he was then Assistant (1965-1968), Associate (1968-1972), and Full Professor of [[Pharmacology]] (1972-1978).

In 1978, he moved to [[Perelman School of Medicine]] at the [[University of Pennsylvania]], where he became director of the diabetes center (until 1998) and professor of [[biochemistry]] and [[biophysics]]. During this time, he was also full professor of these subjects at the school of medicine (1984-1993).

He was active in research and teaching until his retirement in 2021.<ref>{{cite web |title=PSOM 2021 Retiree Slideshow |work=Perelman School of Medicine, University of Pennsylvania |url=https://www.med.upenn.edu/asef/assets/user-content/PSOM%202021%20Retiree%20Slideshow.pdf}}</ref> He died on March 31, 2022, at his home in Wallingford near Philadelphia.

== Research ==

After moving to the US he studied the [[metabolism]] of the [[insulin]]-producing [[pancreatic islets]] and ultimately discovered the essential role of [[glucokinase]] (liver and pancreas hexokinase)<ref>The liver and pancreatic hexokinase D is no more specific for glucose than the other mammalian hexokinase isoenzymes, and strictly the name glucokinase refers to enzymes of bacteria that are highly specific for glucose. However, it is almost universally applied to hexokinase D.</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1042/bj2220363|journal = Biochem. J. | volume = 222|number=2|pages = 363–370|year = 1984|last1 = Cárdenas|first1 = M. L.|last2 = Rabajille|first2 = E. |last3 = Niemeyer| first3 = H.|title = Fructose is a good substrate for rat-liver glucokinase (hexokinase D)|pmid = 6477520 |pmc = 1144187 }}</ref> in the regulation of glucose-stimulated insulin secretion.<ref>Matschinsky FM, Ellerman JE: Metabolism of glucose in islets of Langerhans. J Biol Chem 243:2730-2736, 1968</ref> In subsequent studies, Matschinsky illuminated a role for manipulation of glucokinase in correcting metabolic defects in human pancreatic islet cells and other tissues involved in type 2 diabetes. Current knowledge on the role of glucokinase in the β cell and its misfunction causing diabetes is to a large extent based on work conducted by Matschinsky over the years. He published over 300 papers<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/F-M-Matschinsky-39499801|title=Researchgate: F.M. Matschinsky|access-date=2022-04-29|archive-date=2023-02-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230219011105/https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/F-M-Matschinsky-39499801|url-status=live}}</ref> over his career. He was editor-in-chief of ''[[Diabetes (journal)|Diabetes]]'' (2002 - 2006).<ref>[https://diabetesjournals.org/diabetes/article/56/1/1/12767/New-Editorial-Team-Diabetes-Journal New Editorial Team Diabetes Journal] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220429151343/https://diabetesjournals.org/diabetes/article/56/1/1/12767/New-Editorial-Team-Diabetes-Journal |date=2022-04-29 }} Diabetes 2007;56(1):1–2 https://doi.org/10.2337/db07-9900</ref>

== Awards ==

He has received several awards for his research in the field of insulin secretion and diabetes therapy:

* 1988 [[IDF Medal]] of the [[International Diabetes Federation]]
*     1992 [[Elliott Proctor Joslin Medal]]
*     1994 [[Banting Medal]]<ref>[https://diabetesjournals.org/diabetes/article-pdf/45/2/223/362208/45-2-223.pdf A Lesson in Metabolic Regulation Inspired by the Glucokinase Glucose Sensor Paradigm] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221219053324/https://diabetesjournals.org/diabetes/article-pdf/45/2/223/362208/45-2-223.pdf |date=2022-12-19 }} Banting Lecture 1995</ref>
*     1996 [[Paul Langerhans Medal]]
*     2011 [[Paul Lacy Medal]]
*     2020 [[Rolf Luft Award]]<ref>[https://news.ki.se/professor-franz-matschinsky-receives-the-rolf-luft-award-2020 Professor Franz Matschinsky receives the Rolf Luft Award 2020] [[Karolinska Institute]] Stockholm</ref>
